subject: business-studies
title: Globalisation Drivers and MNCs
welcome_lead: Why has the world shrunk - and what do multinationals do with that?
meta_desc: A-Level Global Business: globalisation drivers and the role of MNCs.
final_note: Globalisation lifts opportunity and risk in equal measure.

concepts.def: Chandler (1962): determination of long-term goals and allocation of resources to achieve them.
Mission states current purpose; vision states future aspiration; both should anchor strategy.
1985: cost leadership, differentiation, focus; firms 'stuck in the middle' underperform.
Kim and Mauborgne (2005): create uncontested market space rather than competing in 'red oceans'; e.g. Cirque du Soleil.
Johnson, Scholes and Whittington: firms become misaligned with environment as historic success blinds management.
Corporate (which markets), business (how to compete), functional (operations) levels of strategic decision.

walkthroughs.body_html: Falling transport costs (containerisation), digital communication, trade liberalisation via the WTO and the rise of emerging markets all combined to shrink distance.
MNCs allocate production across borders to exploit cost differences, skills and tax regimes. They can transfer technology and create jobs - but also dominate local markets and avoid tax.
Long supply chains are vulnerable to pandemics, geopolitics and climate shocks. Many firms are now reshoring or nearshoring to cut these risks.
